P0_quality_certification_feasibility.question: given the current cold-chain state, the candidate route and the known contract, can the fish-salability threshold over execution be certified CONSERVATIVELY at a decision point?
why: quality evolution is a deterministic function of (current VehicleColdChainState, segment durations, compartment-temperature profile, contract)

that very trajectory is ALREADY replayed by c0_completion_energy (run_exp_energy_c0.py:112-151), which drives transition_segment per order and already passes order_quantity / order_temp_class / initial_quality / segment_distance_units / return_to_depot (:132-136, :147-150)
it simply DISCARDS the quality: it returns only cumulative_energy_kwh (:151) and never returns the per-lot quality_remaining
so_the_gap_is: the interface does not expose the replayed per-lot quality

in_force_physics_measured.dataset_initial_quality: 1.0 for ALL three temperature classes (NOT 9 for fish)
in_force_physics_measured.monotonicity: quality is capped by min(previous, decayed) at :405 -> non-increasing in time
in_force_physics_measured.settlement_point: salable is written on the delivery record at depot return, not at the customer

conservativeness.finding: the nominal-schedule replay is an OPTIMISTIC upper bound, not a conservative one, because quality is monotone non-increasing in time
required: evaluate a WORST-CASE admissible schedule (latest TW arrival per customer) rather than the nominal one
keep the FULL wait to booking_horizon (skipping it would be optimistic)
include the committed leg exactly once
per-temperature-class thresholds (class 2 = 0.90 binds first); do not use one global threshold
honour the non-precooled field-temperature branch (coldchain_state.py:398-402) which raises the rate materially

why_not_reuse_evaluate_trace_a1_directly.reason: structural, not merely 'it needs a full trace'
differences: input: real executed traces vs current state + candidate plan
semantics: 'was the delivery salable' vs 'is this plan salable IF executed as planned under a worst-case schedule'
failure meaning: hard-constraint violation vs refusal of the plan's certification
why_not_reuse_evaluate_trace_a1_directly.also: under v1 all three temperature classes have a threshold (the 'tomato is not evaluated' rule is a v2 feature), and evaluate_trace_a1 additionally covers commitment/duplicate/served_not_accepted constraints that belong to OTHER certification components

four_states.callback_invoked: InstallLedger.n_installs == 1 and a receipt exists -- proves ONLY that the callback ran
four_states.suffix_written: per-vehicle list(v.mutable_suffix) == the plan suffix, after replanner.plan and before the commit loop
four_states.head_committed: v.committed_next == plan head and v.status == 'committed' (head 0 -> returning/idle)
four_states.verified_consistent: served_route / trace.services reflect the customer, validate_full_partition passes, and every difference between P_after_install and P_certified is explained

P0_submit_boundary.failure_mode_that_must_be_representable: callback_invoked=True while head_committed=False -- the written suffix is cleared by the next reveal (:528) or the vehicle status is no longer idle/ready so the loop skips it (:651), with NO record today (mechanism demonstrated on a detached copy in B1 C5)
